items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: oh Peter Appleyard played vibes, and one night Lionel came in and sat in with us

ctx.x: I think he did mention that.

And then Lionel Hampton sat in, oh Peter Appleyard played vibes, and one night Lionel came in and sat in with us. And Johnny Mercer came up and sang with us one night. So things like that were happening a lot.
And these days, you split your time between going around to these jazz parties and doing recording. Have you got a recording session planned coming up?

items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: The record I made over in Barbados was done with Bucky, Major Holly, Butch Miles, Rick Wilkins on tenor, and myself, without the piano.

ctx.x: Yeah. Why would a musician be his favorite? Were you able to figure that out?

I really don’t know. Bucky had a very nice personality and his wife is very lovely. I don’t know. Because the one European tour that we did, Bucky was on guitar, he never gave him one solo the whole tour.
Well why would he — conversely why would he fire somebody at a moment’s notice? Do you know?
